collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 35 or older)

collection.description: A villager imagines the self who left Isola with the explorers: wave to the other one, or wonder if they are happy.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Long ago, (name1) had the chance to leave Isola, to go out across the sea with a group of explorers who never came back to stay. (He/she) said no. Today, standing on the beach looking out at the horizon, (he/she) finds (him/her)self imagining the other version of (him/her)self: the one who went. Somewhere out there, living some other life.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (name1) imagines that other self, older now too, standing on some faraway beach, looking back this way and wondering about the one who stayed. (He/she) feels silly. (He/she) waves anyway, at the empty sea. "Hope it's going well," (he/she) says. "It's going fine here." Then (he/she) goes home for dinner, which is fish, which is good.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) wonders if the other version is happy. Happier? Less happy? Just different? (He/she) can't know. Nobody ever can. (He/she) thinks about all the things (he/she) would have missed if (he/she) had gone. Then about all the things (he/she) missed by staying. It comes out about even. That's probably the truth of it. (He/she) picks up a shell and walks home.
